title: Suo Motu & Complete Justice
lead: ==‘Paradoxically, the greatest danger to the administration of justice and constitutional interpretation arises from the genuine desire of Judges to do justice in each individual case’ — H.M. Seervai.== In 2024 the SC exercised ==suo motu jurisdiction in 12 cases — the highest ever==.

items.title: Rationale
bullets: Relief to do ==‘complete justice’ beyond applicable statutory provisions==
Directions filling perceived ==legislative gaps==, operating as ==law of the land== until the legislature or executive steps in
==Do not hold precedent value==

items.title: Judicial Framing
bullets: [[SCBA v. UoI (1998)]]: ==‘a valuable weapon to prevent clogging of the stream of injustice’== — but Art 142 can ==‘supplement’ but not ‘supplant’== substantive law
[[Pravasi Bhalai Sangathan v. UoI (2014)]]: for a direction to be effective there must be an ==implementation mechanism==
==IIM-Ahmedabad (May 2024)==: of ==1,579 SC cases== invoking ‘Article 142’ or ‘complete justice’, usage was ==ambiguous in almost 40%==

items.title: Pros
bullets: ==Equitable justice== — Union Carbide compensation (1989) for Bhopal victims
==Systemic reforms== — [[Lakshmi Kant Pandey v. UoI (1984)]] regulating inter-country adoptions
==Ensures complete justice== — Perarivalan case (2022)
Protects public interest — [[SaveLIFE Foundation v. UoI (2016)]]

items.title: Cons
bullets: ==Unchecked authority== — [[Reliance Natural Resources v. Reliance Industries (2010)]] effectively ==rewriting contracts==
==Legal uncertainty== — Coal Block allocation cancellations (2014) disrupting industries

blocks.text: As long as there are intersections between law and public life, there will be a place for the Court's discretionary power under Article 142. And as long as the rule of law prevails, there will be calls to use it sparingly.

items.title: Methods
bullets: Action against a person who shows ==contempt==
==Transfer a case== to itself or to lower courts on its own will
==Cognisance of pressing issues== affecting society

items.title: Pros
bullets: ==Urgent intervention== — COVID-19 migrant crisis
==Public interest== — rights of deaf students, prisoners, marginalised groups otherwise unnoticed

items.title: Cons
bullets: ==Selective justice== — depends on individual judges' priorities
==Procedural risks== — may lack proper notice and hearing; due-process concerns
==Judicial overreach== into executive/legislative domains

items.title: Examples
bullets: ==Manipur violence==
Lokpal HC judge ambit
==Ganga cleanliness==
Sariska Tiger Reserve
==Kolkata hospital case==

blocks.text: ==Arts 32 and 226 and the growth of PILs== have widened the scope of suo motu matters heard by constitutional courts.
